heading: Two pointers eliminate impossible pairs
body:
In a **sorted** array, start pointers at both ends.

- Sum too **small**? Move left → (bigger number)
- Sum too **large**? Move right ← (smaller number)

Each move eliminates an entire class of pairs. **O(n) time, O(1) space.**

heading: Why sortedness matters
body:
Moving a pointer changes the sum **predictably**:
- Left pointer → always increases sum
- Right pointer ← always decreases sum

Without sorting, you can't decide which pointer to move.

label: Crux · Python

q: Why does the two-pointer approach only work on a sorted array?
options: Because sorting reduces the time complexity to O(1)
Because we need the array length to be even
Because sortedness guarantees that moving a pointer changes the sum predictably in one direction
Because unsorted arrays cannot contain pairs that sum to a target
explain: In a sorted array, moving the left pointer right always increases the sum, and moving the right pointer left always decreases the sum.
